title: Food Truck Circus
subtitle: A fan game after Cirque Kikasse's SANTÉ!, the circus played on a food truck, made for its Durham run in October 2026.
no_webgl: This browser has no WebGL 2, which the game draws with.
about: Cirque Kikasse is a circus company from Québec. In SANTÉ! its performers bounce off a trampoline beside their food truck, stack tables and chairs into a tower about thirty-five feet high, juggle, clean up badly on purpose, and let the popcorn machine overflow. This game is a tribute, not their show: every stop on the map is a real venue from their 2025–26 tour, and the trapeze is the game's own addition.
map_hint: Pick a show. A show opens when the ones before it on the map are done.
locked: Finish the shows before this one first.

lab.blocked_wasm: The Circus Math Lab cannot start on this device: its settings block WebAssembly, which the lab runs on. A school's IT team can allow WebAssembly for sgilson7.github.io (in Chrome, the JavaScript JIT setting).
lab.blocked_webgl: This device blocks WebGL, which draws the performer, so the stage stays empty. A school's IT team can allow WebGL for sgilson7.github.io (in Chrome, the 3D APIs setting).
lab.title: Circus Math Lab
lab.subtitle: Three labs where a circus performer does the mathematics: a function plotted by bouncing, the area under a flight counted in popcorn, and juggling patterns written as numbers.
lab.open: Graph Lab: plot a function by bouncing
lab.draw_hint: Drag a point up or down. The line through the points is your function.
lab.table_hint: Put x in, get f(x) out. Then look at how much f(x) changes from one row to the next.
lab.you_hint: Hold Space to bounce higher, C to come down. Hold → while the trampoline throws you to lean right, ← to lean left. Every top you reach is marked.
lab.plan_hint: A behaviour tree: the lit nodes are running. The performer presses only keys you could press, and chooses how long by imagining bounces first.
ideas: Watch the feet between two marks. What shape is every flight? Does it matter what function you asked for?
Look at the change column for x². Then the change of the change. Try 2x+1, and x³. What do you notice?
Draw a function the performer cannot plot. What makes it impossible?
Plot x² with 3 points, then 5, then 17. When does the line through the marks look like the curve?
Ask for |x|. Where does the performer have to work hardest, and why there?
The performer guesses a push, imagines it, and tries a number in between. How would you choose the next guess?
Join the marks with straight lines, then a smooth curve. Which is closer to x²? Is it closer for |x| too?
lab.summary: {n} points plotted. On average each mark was {cm} cm off in the air, {units} on the graph.
lab.domain_order: The first number has to be smaller than the second.

tree.trick: Choose a trick for the flight

log.read: Next: x = {x}. The machine says f({x}) = {y}.
log.imagine_push: Imagine pushing for {beats} beats: the top would be at {y}.
log.imagine_stop: Imagine stopping the trampoline for {beats} beats: the top would be at {y}.
log.between: {y} is between {a} beats ({ya}) and {b} beats ({yb}), {pct}% of the way. Try {u}.
log.set_up: {y} is too far for one bounce. A set-up bounce first.
log.imagine_lean: Imagine leaning for {beats} beats: the top lands at x = {x}.
log.lean_between: Aim for x = {x}: try leaning {w} beats.
log.marked: Marked ({x}, {y}). The machine said f({fx}) = {fy}: off by {off}.
log.no_value: f({x}) has no value ({why}). Skip it.
log.bow: Every point is marked. Come down and bow.
log.imagine_flip: Imagine holding {key} for {beats} beats: {deg}° of somersault by the landing.
log.flip_between: One whole somersault is 360°: try {beats} beats.
log.trick: A {trick} on the way up and down. The mark is where the feet would be standing, so the trick does not move it.

expr.end: The formula stops too soon. Something is missing at the end.
expr.bar: A | is missing to close the absolute value (at character {at}).
expr.unknown: I don't know the name “{word}”. Use x, and sin, cos, tan, abs, sqrt, floor, round, pi.

undefined.fraction_power: no value: only whole powers and ^0.5

lab.join_heading: How close is the performer's version?
lab.join_hint: The orange line joins the marks: the performer's version of f. The shaded gap is how far it is from f.
lab.error_lines: Joined with straight lines, the performer's version is at most {max} from f (at x = {at}), and {mean} off on average.
lab.error_smooth: Joined with a smooth curve, the performer's version is at most {max} from f (at x = {at}), and {mean} off on average.
lab.fly_intro: The performer jumps off the ledge, lands on the trampoline and bounces on to the grass. The flight draws a curve. In every strip of ground the performer drops a column of popcorn as tall as they are high at that moment: the piles add up the area under the curve.
lab.fly_arcs_hint: From where it leaves the ledge or the trampoline and how fast, each arc of the flight has an equation. The second form shows the top of the arc.
lab.fly_kernel: One kernel is a square ¼ m by ¼ m: 1/16 of a square metre.
lab.fly_summary: {kernels} kernels of popcorn: {popcorn} m². The Riemann sum (the piles' heights times {width} m) is {riemann} m². The area under the flight, worked out finely, is {fine} m².
lab.fly_numbers: Each of the three must be a number.
lab.fly_no_start: The curve has no value at the ledge (x = -4.6).
lab.fly_ledge_moved: The ledge only goes from 3 to 8 m, so it is set at {h} m.
lab.fly_match_hint: Type a curve in x (metres along the ground, the ledge's edge at x = -4.6). The performer finds the jump whose flight fits it best: they imagine jumps and fit a parabola through how far off three of them are, to find the best one.

fly_log.try_speed: At {speed} m/s, the best angle is about {angle}°: off by {off} m.
fly_log.parabola: Fit a parabola through the misfits at {l}° and {r}°: its lowest point says try {next}°.
fly_log.fit: Best: {speed} m/s at {angle}°, off by {off} m on average.

fly_ideas: Jump at the same speed with a bigger angle. What happens to the number in front of (x + 4.6)²? Why does the angle not change it?
Make the strips narrower. Do the popcorn and the area under the flight get closer?
Drop at the start, the middle, then the end of each strip. Which comes closest? Which is always too much on the way down?
Type a curve that opens upward, like 0.3(x+1)^2+2. Can any jump draw it? Why not?
The second arc starts on the trampoline. Is its equation's first number always about 1?
lab.jug_intro: A juggler throws on a steady beat, the hands taking turns. Each number says how many beats a ball stays up: a 3 comes down three beats later, a 5 five beats later and much higher. A 2 is a ball held, a 0 an empty hand. The pattern repeats.
lab.jug_ok: {digits} = {sum}, over {n} beats: an average of {balls}, so this pattern needs {balls} balls.
lab.jug_average: The throws add up to {sum} over {n} beats: an average of {avg}. No juggler has {avg} balls.
lab.jug_collision: The ball thrown on beat {a} and the ball thrown on beat {b} both come down on beat {lands}: two balls into one hand at once.
lab.jug_digit: Only the digits 0 to 9: “{ch}” at character {at}.
lab.jug_empty: Type a pattern of digits, like 441.
lab.jug_diagram_hint: Each dot is a beat. Each arc goes from a throw to the beat it comes down on, as high as the throw; each colour is one ball.
jug_ideas: Why must the numbers average to a whole number? Try 43.
441 and 531 both use three balls. Find another three-number pattern for three balls.
Change one digit of 441. Which changes still work?
What does a 2 do? Try 330 and 423.
Find a pattern where one ball goes much higher than the rest.
Odd numbers cross from hand to hand and even numbers come back to the same hand. Why?
lab.plot_intro: Give the performer a function. The top of every bounce marks a point on its graph.

moves_heading: Moves, and how to do them
moves_intro: Every trick the crowd can name. A trick is named by where it starts and ends (feet, seat, back or front), how many times you turn over, how many times you twist, and the shape you hold: tucked, piked or straight.
